cards.headline:
Ambient AI documentation
in the eye clinic
cards.body: Ambient AI note-taking cut eye consultation time by up to 37%, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 reached 98.4% EMR accuracy.

blocks.x: EMR documentation contributes to physician workload and reduced patient–physician interaction, with ophthalmology particularly affected by specialist data requirements. This study compared ambient AI-assisted documentation for structured EMR import with conventional entry in standardised ophthalmic consultations.

Ten standardised ophthalmic scenarios were performed under classic and AI-assisted conditions by a consultant and a resident. ChatGPT 5.3 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 used TurboScribe transcription followed by structured LLM output; Heidi 2.0.1 used an integrated audio pipeline. All targeted structured import into an ophthalmic EMR (Heyex; Heidelberg Engineering).

blocks.cap: Fig. 1: Consultation time components: classic versus AI-assisted documentation.

blocks.x: AI-assisted documentation reduced total consultation time by 2.4 min (−32%) for the consultant and 3.0 min (−37%) for the resident. Documentation and review time decreased by 85% and 86%, and off-patient gaze time by 83% and 86%; computer-related gaze shifts decreased by 72% for both clinicians.

blocks.cap: Fig. 2: Item-level distribution of documentation accuracy ratings by AI system.

blocks.x: Accuracy was highest for Claude Sonnet 4.6 (98.4 ± 2.9%), followed by ChatGPT 5.3 (97.0 ± 5.1%) and Heidi 2.0.1 (88.6 ± 9.9%). As only one consultant and one resident were assessed, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.
